title: Depth under pullback by an embedding
statement: Let $e$ be an embedding of the coordinates of a finite cube of dimension $m$ into one of dimension $n$. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets of available coordinates in the two cubes such that, for every coordinate $i$ of the first cube, $i$ belongs to $S$ exactly when $e(i)$ belongs to $T$. For any binary decision tree on $T$, its pullback along $e$ has depth at most the original tree's depth.
